meta.title: Pulsar Kids — learning games for kids aged 4–10
meta.description: Pulsar Kids is a playful learning platform where children aged 4–10 master math, geography, history and ecology — in English. No ads, no tears, no timers: a mistake is just a hint, and parents stay in charge of screen time.

meta.ogDescription: Math, language, logic, geography, astronomy, history and nature in 50 games. Your child plays and builds a planet of their own, while you stay in charge of screen time.

ld.siteDescription: Learning games for kids aged 4–10: math, language, logic, geography, astronomy, history, nature, ecology and art.
ld.browser: A modern browser on a phone, tablet or computer

hero.title: Learning that feels like an adventure
hero.lead: Pulsar Kids turns math, geography, history and ecology into games your child will ask to play. No ads, no losing, no scary timers — just the joy of getting it right. And you stay calmly in charge of screen time.
hero.note: It takes a minute: a parent creates the child’s profile, and the child signs in to the game with a nickname and a PIN.
hero.systemLabel: The Solar System: the Sun and the eight planets your child travels through

about.title: Why Pulsar Kids
about.sub: We want children to want to learn — all by themselves. Most learning apps punish a mistake: they take away a “life”, start a timer, flash a red cross. Children grow afraid of getting it wrong and give up. We did the opposite.

hint.title: A mistake is a hint
hint.text: Nobody loses here. After a mistake a visual hint appears, and the task that didn’t work out comes back once more at the end of the level — to make it stick, not to punish.

voice.title: Play before you can read
voice.text: Tasks and answers are read aloud, and every text has a speaker button next to it. Once your child reads confidently, you can switch the voice off.

steps.title: Difficulty grows with your child
steps.text: Every game is a path of steps, each a little harder than the one before. The stars on a card tell you what age the game is for.

ads.title: No ads
ads.text: No third-party ads and no in-app purchases. Your child sees only the tasks, their own world and their own achievements.

games.title: 50 games across nine galaxies
games.sub: Here subjects are galaxies and games are planets. This is what awaits on them.

math.2: Fractions on pizzas and cakes, and sums with fractions
math.3: A balance scale for numbers and a number maze
math.5: The shop: counting money and change
math.6: Greater, less, equal — and a clock with hands
math.7: Story problems: the shop, friends, the road
math.title: Math

language.1: The alphabet: put the letters in their places in the table
language.2: Letter bubbles, word chains, rhymes and sentences
language.3: Five games in English, and the same five in Ukrainian and in Polish — each with a voice of its own
language.title: Language

logic.1: Rhythm and patterns: what comes next
logic.2: Shadow lotto: find the shadow of the thing
logic.3: Mirror symmetry: the other half of the picture
logic.4: Logic riddles: 150 kinds of puzzles that make you think
logic.title: Logic

astronomy.1: Parade of planets: their order from the Sun, their sizes and a hundred questions about them
astronomy.2: Constellations: join the stars by numbers and letters, then find them in the night sky
astronomy.title: Astronomy

art.1: Color mixer: two paints make a new color
art.title: Art

geography.1: The flags of every country in the world — starting with the best known
geography.3: The oceans on a map of the world
geography.4: Natural zones and the animals that live there
geography.5: Capitals — and why it is day in one place and night in another
geography.title: Geography

history.1: “Time Machine”: 100 tasks about what came first
history.2: 50 dinosaurs: what to feed them and how to tell them apart
history.3: Great people of the world and of Ukraine
history.4: Inventions of the world and of Ukraine
history.title: History

ecology.1: “Eco Patrol”: sorting glass, paper and plastic
ecology.2: Finding out what they will be turned into
ecology.3: “Why is that?”: air, water, climate, animals, energy
ecology.title: Ecology

nature.1: The seasons: what happens in nature and when
nature.title: Nature

world.title: A planet of their own that keeps growing
world.sub: Every task earns crystals. What to do with them is your child’s own decision — and that is a little lesson too.

build.title: Build a world
build.text: Crystals can be traded for buildings and decorations for their own planet. The grandest of all — the “dream castle” — unlocks last.

goal.title: Or save up for a family goal
goal.text: You agree on a real-life reward together: “collect 500 crystals and we bake cookies”. Spend now or keep saving — the choice is your child’s.

stations.title: Stations of knowledge
stations.text: Every new step in any game earns a key of knowledge. The keys open stations on the planet: an observatory, a library, a laboratory of numbers.

theme.title: A favorite theme
theme.text: Unicorns, space, dinosaurs, the underwater world, bricks, the forest, winter… A theme changes the colors, the hero, the crystals and the city that grows on the planet.

parents.sub: A separate entrance for grown-ups. Your child can’t wander in — the game simply has no door to it.

time.title: Screen time without tears
time.text: You set the session length, the break and the daily limit. Your child sees no timer — just hourglasses that slowly disappear. A level already started is always finished, and then the hero “goes for a rest”.

children.title: Up to five children
children.text: Each child has their own profile, nickname and PIN, their own theme, progress and settings.

goals.title: Family goals
goals.text: Agree on real-life rewards and watch your child get closer to them.

settings.title: Settings that fit your child
settings.text: Sound, voice, labels, read-aloud buttons, the number of answer options, the step in every game.

open.title: A parent opens the parents’ area
open.text: Sign in with your email and tap “Add a child”.

nick.title: Sets a nickname and a PIN
nick.text: Think of a simple nickname and a short PIN for your child, and set the play time.

play.title: The child signs in and plays
play.text: On the game page they type their nickname and PIN, then pick a theme and their first planet.

feedback.title: Spotted a bug or have an idea?
feedback.sub: Write to us: what went wrong, what could be handier, which game is missing. You can add a photo or a short video — it makes things easier to understand.

final.title: Ready for the adventure?
final.adult: I’m a grown-up — to the parents’ area

footer.tagline: Learning that feels like an adventure.

js.tooShort: Please write at least a few words.
js.tooLong: The message is too long — please shorten it to 4000 characters.
js.badEmail: Please check the email address: there seems to be a mistake in it.
js.tooMany: You have already sent several messages in a row. Please try again in an hour.
js.notMedia: “{name}” doesn’t look like a photo or a video.
js.maxFiles: You can add no more than {max} files.
js.tooBig: “{name}” is {size}, and the limit is 15 MB. Try a shorter video.
js.noRoom: “{name}” no longer fits: the total limit is 18 MB.
js.filesLost: We received your text, but not all the files arrived — the connection seems to have let us down. If they matter, please send them again.
js.willReply: We will read it and reply to the address you gave.
js.thanks: We read every message. Thank you for helping us make the game better.
js.failed: It could not be sent. Check your connection and try again.
